Next I'm testing a task that has two new rules but is more similar to the trained tasks than the recombined task is. This puts the two hypotheses' predictions in opposite directions.
The ordering so far tracks how many rules are new to the learner, not similarity. I'm adding samples to firm that up, including a second recombined task.

Results have stayed in the noisy 20-30 example range throughout, even for the already-trained task, suggesting any effect is small relative to noise. I'll use the remaining 10 budget units on a final contrast comparing frequently-seen versus rarely-seen rules while keeping similarity matched.

content.text:
I submitted **factor-when-justified** with confidence **0.4**. That is only a little above the 1/3 prior: the noise was too large to tell the three hypotheses apart with any confidence. I used the whole budget of 60.

**Noise.** Almost every test came back between about 10 and 35 examples, whatever the conditions. Even L2-S2-M2, a task the learner had already been trained on, gave 27, 54 and 22.

**Phase 1:** I trained L1-S1-M1, L2-S2-M2 and L3-S3-M3, so each rule had been seen once.

| Task | New rules | Highest similarity to a trained task | Mean examples (samples) |
|---|---|---|---|
| L3-S1-M2 | 0 | 0.375 | 16 (8) |
| L2-S1-M3 | 0 | 0.375 | 25 (5) |
| L1-S4-M1 | 1 | 0.625 | 19 (3) |
| L4-S4-M1 | 2 | 0.5625 | 26 (7) |
| L4-S4-M4 | 3 | 0.1875 | 26.5 (8) |

- **Against part-based:** L2-S1-M3 has no new rules but cost about the same as the all-new task.
- **Weakly against holistic:** L4-S4-M1 was more similar to the trained tasks than the recombined ones, yet it was not cheaper. Factor-when-justified behaves the same as holistic at this stage, so this counts against it too.

**Phase 2:** I trained 7 more tasks so that L4, S4 and M4 each appeared 3 times, while keeping L4-S4-M4 itself fairly dissimilar from everything trained (highest similarity 0.375). I had meant to train 6; one extra slipped in, which did no harm.
- **Weakly against factor-when-justified:** L4-S4-M4's mean only moved from 26.5 to 23.5, smaller than the drop this hypothesis predicts.
- **For factor-when-justified (the one result that points to it):** I compared two tasks with similar similarity to the trained set.
  - L3-S1-M1, whose rules had each appeared 3 or more times, gave a mean of 15 and a median of 8.
  - L2-S3-M3, whose rules had appeared only once or twice, gave a mean of 27 and a median of 17.
  - With only 5 samples each and this much noise, this is weak evidence.

Overall each hypothesis has at least one result against it. Factor-when-justified came out slightly ahead, mainly because of that last contrast.
